course_name_original: Elasticidad Y Resistencia De Materiales Ii
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II
prerequisites: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales I

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: The elastic problem: formulation and solution
Plane reticulated systems with articulated nodes
Failure criteria. Study of solids subjected to plastic deformations
teaching_methods: Practice of a large number of practical exercises
Voluntary laboratory practices (attendance and submission of results sheets)
Learning (reading and comprehension) of basic bibliography text
Self-assessment activities (solving self-check exercises, completing Continuous Assessment Tests)
assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as follows: If Continuous Assessment Tests (PECs) are not submitted, NF equals the Exam Grade (NE). If PECs are submitted, NF is calculated as 0.2 times the PEC Grade (NPECs) plus 0.8 times the Exam Grade (NE). A minimum grade of 4 on the exam is required for the PEC grade to be added to the final calculation. The maximum final grade (10) can be obtained solely from the in-person exam. Voluntary laboratory practices will be considered in case of doubt.
